fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA in its as-cast FCC+B2 state.
It substitutes HPHT processing for intermediate-temperature aging at approximately 600°C and 750°C.
It predicts simultaneous strength–ductility improvement rather than a non-monotonic ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
The proposed deformation mechanism omits enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and phase-boundary-tip stress concentration.
The stated room-temperature-to-1600°C boundary is unrelated to the approximately 550–750°C embrittlement window.
The cited evidence supports HPHT-induced strength–ductility synergy in an EHEA but does not support thermally induced ductile–brittle–ductile behavior.
explanation: The response recognizes eutectic high-entropy alloys as a relevant broad material class, but it reconstructs a different study and phenomenon. Its HPHT treatment, coherent-interface microstructure, multimechanism plasticity, and improved strength–ductility outcome are scientifically plausible and partly supported by E1, yet they do not answer why AlCoCrFeNi2.1 undergoes aging-induced embrittlement near 600°C and ductility recovery near 750°C. E2 and E3 provide only general HEA background and do not establish the claimed transition. The proposed experiment could test HPHT strengthening but cannot discriminate the target ordering- and phase-boundary-mediated mechanism.
